1.name: Table_legends
rows: The supporting tables describe the tissue and expression contributing to each tumor-adjacent versus distant stromal comparison. The regional contrast is the median expression among near spots minus the median among far spots. Its exploratory four-gene readout is the arithmetic mean of log1p CP10K expression for TGFB1, CXCL12, ACTA2 and TAGLN. “Expression units” refer to this mean or the named component. Standardized values divide by the median absolute deviation (MAD) across all annotated pure stromal spots in the section. A zero MAD makes standardized values undefined; expression-unit estimates remain available when the tissue requirements are met.
See Table_legends and Field_dictionary for definitions.

The supporting tables describe the tissue and expression contributing to each tumor-adjacent versus distant stromal comparison. The regional contrast is the median expression among near spots minus the median among far spots. Its exploratory four-gene readout is the arithmetic mean of log1p CP10K expression for TGFB1, CXCL12, ACTA2 and TAGLN. “Expression units” refer to this mean or the named component. Standardized values divide by the median absolute deviation (MAD) across all annotated pure stromal spots in the section. A zero MAD makes standardized values undefined; expression-unit estimates remain available when the tissue requirements are met.

The 22 attempted sections represent 12 patients; the baseline domain-selected comparisons draw on five patients per resource. Patient counts remain the unit of biological replication across maps, sections, graphs and sensitivity settings. Tables report the observations contributing to each contrast, standardized estimate or whole-domain geometry. Complete row grids retain unavailable attempts, with status fields indicating the tissue or fitting requirements and NA indicating missing or inapplicable quantities. The field dictionary defines columns, units and missing values.
Patient variation in the effect of domain selection and location matching.

The patient summaries compare selected and full-band contrasts with random subsets matched for size or coarse location. They show the variation underlying the resource medians and the influence of individual patients. primary_patient_summary.tsv includes all 12 attempted patients under each selection rule, including those lacking regional estimates. Contrasts, absolute deviations and control-median offsets are summarized across partitions within method/K, method/K settings within sections, and sections within patients; settings and sections receive equal weight at their respective steps. Standardized availability is recorded separately. configuration_location_matching_summary.tsv counts decreases, increases and ties among all 407 primary baseline configurations, by resource and overall. The configurations are repeated measurements within patients. patient_leave_one_out.tsv gives size- and location-matched resource medians and their difference after omitting each patient, leaving four contributing patient summaries. The patient summaries for maps eligible for comparison with their default maps under the fixed criteria based on image-pixel distances are in diagnostic_patient_summary.tsv; both selection rules reuse the patients.
Patient variation in the effect of domain selection and location matching.

The reference-precision records quantify uncertainty from the finite number of random subsets. They contain 407 map records, ten patient records and two resource records in control_reference_map_precision.tsv, control_reference_patient_precision.tsv and control_reference_resource_precision.tsv. The bounds have at least 95% simultaneous coverage over 814 control medians, quantifying Monte Carlo precision with the observed tissue, readout and maps held fixed. Resource gaps are differences between resource medians; patient gaps are differences between that patient's summaries.

2.name: Table_legends
rows: The supporting tables describe the tissue and expression contributing to each tumor-adjacent versus distant stromal comparison. The regional contrast is the median expression among near spots minus the median among far spots. Its exploratory four-gene readout is the arithmetic mean of log1p CP10K expression for TGFB1, CXCL12, ACTA2 and TAGLN. “Expression units” refer to this mean or the named component. Standardized values divide by the median absolute deviation (MAD) across all annotated pure stromal spots in the section. A zero MAD makes standardized values undefined; expression-unit estimates remain available when the tissue requirements are met.
See Table_legends and Field_dictionary for definitions.

The supporting tables describe the tissue and expression contributing to each tumor-adjacent versus distant stromal comparison. The regional contrast is the median expression among near spots minus the median among far spots. Its exploratory four-gene readout is the arithmetic mean of log1p CP10K expression for TGFB1, CXCL12, ACTA2 and TAGLN. “Expression units” refer to this mean or the named component. Standardized values divide by the median absolute deviation (MAD) across all annotated pure stromal spots in the section. A zero MAD makes standardized values undefined; expression-unit estimates remain available when the tissue requirements are met.

The 22 attempted sections represent 12 patients; the baseline domain-selected comparisons draw on five patients per resource. Patient counts remain the unit of biological replication across maps, sections, graphs and sensitivity settings. Tables report the observations contributing to each contrast, standardized estimate or whole-domain geometry. Complete row grids retain unavailable attempts, with status fields indicating the tissue or fitting requirements and NA indicating missing or inapplicable quantities. The field dictionary defines columns, units and missing values.
Tissue context and contractile expression underlying the case contrasts.

Registered tissue locations and local transcript distributions describe the contractile expression contributing to the case contrasts. case_section_geometry.tsv describes the five case sections under each graph. case_block_contributions.tsv supplies counts and component medians within each band, readout, setting and spatial block. Block medians describe local distributions; regional contrasts use pooled-spot medians. Annotation coverage for all 22 sections is in source_label_coverage.tsv, which separates missing source labels from annotated but unresolved tissue. Patient6's original Layer1/Layer2/Layer3 records and coverage details are in additional_source_data/. Fig S3 uses all 9,530 positions and the baseline masks in figure_source_data/figureS7_spots.tsv.gz. Positions lacking source classes retain an unknown annotation.
Tissue context and contractile expression underlying the case contrasts.

Three additional markers, MYH11, CNN1 and DES, extend the contractile examination across all 22 sections. contractile_marker_section_summary.tsv reports spot counts, detection fractions, medians, quartiles and near-minus-far differences for every section and gene. contractile_marker_block_summary.tsv covers every occupied near or far block, and contractile_marker_spots.tsv.gz gives registered values and unchanged memberships. Detection fractions use all spots in the stated group; empty-group expression summaries are undefined. The values are in log-normalized expression units. These measurements locate contractile transcripts within the deposited stromal classes, at the resolution of the original tissue annotations.

3.name: Table_legends
rows: The supporting tables describe the tissue and expression contributing to each tumor-adjacent versus distant stromal comparison. The regional contrast is the median expression among near spots minus the median among far spots. Its exploratory four-gene readout is the arithmetic mean of log1p CP10K expression for TGFB1, CXCL12, ACTA2 and TAGLN. “Expression units” refer to this mean or the named component. Standardized values divide by the median absolute deviation (MAD) across all annotated pure stromal spots in the section. A zero MAD makes standardized values undefined; expression-unit estimates remain available when the tissue requirements are met.
See Table_legends and Field_dictionary for definitions.

The supporting tables describe the tissue and expression contributing to each tumor-adjacent versus distant stromal comparison. The regional contrast is the median expression among near spots minus the median among far spots. Its exploratory four-gene readout is the arithmetic mean of log1p CP10K expression for TGFB1, CXCL12, ACTA2 and TAGLN. “Expression units” refer to this mean or the named component. Standardized values divide by the median absolute deviation (MAD) across all annotated pure stromal spots in the section. A zero MAD makes standardized values undefined; expression-unit estimates remain available when the tissue requirements are met.

The 22 attempted sections represent 12 patients; the baseline domain-selected comparisons draw on five patients per resource. Patient counts remain the unit of biological replication across maps, sections, graphs and sensitivity settings. Tables report the observations contributing to each contrast, standardized estimate or whole-domain geometry. Complete row grids retain unavailable attempts, with status fields indicating the tissue or fitting requirements and NA indicating missing or inapplicable quantities. The field dictionary defines columns, units and missing values.
Original-count measurements underlying the component comparisons.

One record per attempted section connects original gene counts with the registered spots used for regional expression. component_source_recovery.tsv gives source feature and barcode counts, full-feature CP10K/log1p normalization, source-file identities, barcode alignment and the error when the four-gene mean is recomposed. This correspondence places the single-gene measurements on the same expression scale as the regional outcome.

4.name: Table_legends
rows: The supporting tables describe the tissue and expression contributing to each tumor-adjacent versus distant stromal comparison. The regional contrast is the median expression among near spots minus the median among far spots. Its exploratory four-gene readout is the arithmetic mean of log1p CP10K expression for TGFB1, CXCL12, ACTA2 and TAGLN. “Expression units” refer to this mean or the named component. Standardized values divide by the median absolute deviation (MAD) across all annotated pure stromal spots in the section. A zero MAD makes standardized values undefined; expression-unit estimates remain available when the tissue requirements are met.
See Table_legends and Field_dictionary for definitions.

The supporting tables describe the tissue and expression contributing to each tumor-adjacent versus distant stromal comparison. The regional contrast is the median expression among near spots minus the median among far spots. Its exploratory four-gene readout is the arithmetic mean of log1p CP10K expression for TGFB1, CXCL12, ACTA2 and TAGLN. “Expression units” refer to this mean or the named component. Standardized values divide by the median absolute deviation (MAD) across all annotated pure stromal spots in the section. A zero MAD makes standardized values undefined; expression-unit estimates remain available when the tissue requirements are met.

The 22 attempted sections represent 12 patients; the baseline domain-selected comparisons draw on five patients per resource. Patient counts remain the unit of biological replication across maps, sections, graphs and sensitivity settings. Tables report the observations contributing to each contrast, standardized estimate or whole-domain geometry. Complete row grids retain unavailable attempts, with status fields indicating the tissue or fitting requirements and NA indicating missing or inapplicable quantities. The field dictionary defines columns, units and missing values.
Direct readout-feature inclusion affects both selected expression and regional coverage.

New fits of expression k-means, coordinate-augmented k-means, spatial Ward and spatial Leiden compare versions allowing or withholding TGFB1, CXCL12, ACTA2 and TAGLN. The allowed version permits these genes among variance-selected features; the withheld version excludes every source feature with these symbols. Both use the same fitting denominator over the other features, and actual feature ranks identify which genes entered each section's principal-component analysis (PCA). The regional outcome retains full-feature normalization. The paired fitting results contain 1,056 attempts across 528 paired configurations and their section arrays. The feature-withholding comparison is confined to these four methods; the other domain maps enter the primary analysis.
Direct readout-feature inclusion affects both selected expression and regional coverage.

The primary comparison uses the same settings with sufficient near and far tissue in both versions. map_results.tsv separates fitting success from regional availability: 1,042 of 1,056 attempts attained the requested domain number, while 14 Leiden attempts did not attain exact K. paired_map_results.tsv identifies 204 configurations meeting spot and block requirements in both versions, comprising 76 Valdeolivas and 128 GSE294385. Withholding gained 19 and lost five usable configurations in Valdeolivas, and gained five and lost three in GSE294385. The arm_specific summaries in patient_summary.tsv, section_summary.tsv and resource_summary.tsv include all usable settings and preserve unavailable attempted patients. Successive medians give equal weight to replicates within method/K, settings within sections, sections within patients and patients within resources. n_evaluable_maps counts repeated configurations within the patients contributing to each version and frame.
Direct readout-feature inclusion affects both selected expression and regional coverage.

Membership overlap and regional expression have different contributing sets. Selected-stroma Jaccard uses all selected annotated stromal members, including those outside the bands; band Jaccard uses retained near and far members. Whole-map adjusted Rand index compares all registered labels. These metrics require valid fits and mapped domains but can remain calculable without sufficient regional tissue. Each usable version/configuration receives 1,000 size-matched and 1,000 location-matched subsets, with version excluded from the random-seed context. Difference fields are withheld minus allowed, in the same expression or MAD units as the main comparison. Fitted labels, PCA inputs, masks and complete subset draws accompany the table. Regional results are point contrasts and reference summaries. With fitting normalization and regional measurement held constant, the pairs measure how direct feature inclusion affects selection and expression in these four families. Both versions retain the observed expression correlations and tissue composition.

5.name: Table_legends
rows: The supporting tables describe the tissue and expression contributing to each tumor-adjacent versus distant stromal comparison. The regional contrast is the median expression among near spots minus the median among far spots. Its exploratory four-gene readout is the arithmetic mean of log1p CP10K expression for TGFB1, CXCL12, ACTA2 and TAGLN. “Expression units” refer to this mean or the named component. Standardized values divide by the median absolute deviation (MAD) across all annotated pure stromal spots in the section. A zero MAD makes standardized values undefined; expression-unit estimates remain available when the tissue requirements are met.
See Table_legends and Field_dictionary for definitions.

The supporting tables describe the tissue and expression contributing to each tumor-adjacent versus distant stromal comparison. The regional contrast is the median expression among near spots minus the median among far spots. Its exploratory four-gene readout is the arithmetic mean of log1p CP10K expression for TGFB1, CXCL12, ACTA2 and TAGLN. “Expression units” refer to this mean or the named component. Standardized values divide by the median absolute deviation (MAD) across all annotated pure stromal spots in the section. A zero MAD makes standardized values undefined; expression-unit estimates remain available when the tissue requirements are met.

The 22 attempted sections represent 12 patients; the baseline domain-selected comparisons draw on five patients per resource. Patient counts remain the unit of biological replication across maps, sections, graphs and sensitivity settings. Tables report the observations contributing to each contrast, standardized estimate or whole-domain geometry. Complete row grids retain unavailable attempts, with status fields indicating the tissue or fitting requirements and NA indicating missing or inapplicable quantities. The field dictionary defines columns, units and missing values.
Contrast magnitude, uncertainty and classification across regional definitions.

The continuous estimates show how domain selection changes a contrast; the secondary support rules show how its interpretation depends on a magnitude margin and interval. corrected_full_effects.tsv contains 16,800 records, crossing the 1,680-combination grid with two graphs and five settings. Full-band, selected-domain and paired-change intervals use the spatial-block bootstrap in Supporting Methods. real_threshold_sensitivity.tsv applies margins of 0, 0.25, 0.50 and 0.75 MAD to these estimates and supplies the counts meeting each descriptive rule. setting_status_summary.tsv reports baseline availability. geometry_result_reconciliation.tsv compares band membership, selected counts and continuous estimates under the image-coordinate and nominal-array conventions; each convention is identified in the table.

6.name: Table_legends
rows: Supplementary Table S6: Whole-domain purity, fine clustering and regional coverage
The following explanation applies to all data worksheets in this workbook.
Whole-domain purity, fine clustering and regional coverage

Whole-domain purity is the fraction of coarse-annotated stromal spots among all spots in the selected primary region; unknown and other annotations remain in the denominator. Purity and primary eligibility are different: primary_evaluable requires both selected near and far intersections to contain at least 20 stromal spots and at least 3 distinct spatial blocks. any_pure_region_evaluable describes availability among any pure region and is an upper-bound availability measure, not the primary selection. requested_K is nominal; actual_fitted_K is reported separately and can exceed it when disconnected graph components each receive at least one cluster. The primary selection is the largest pure connected region, chosen without its regional expression contrast. Adjacent regions merge only under the stated purity and centroid-distance criteria, using the 25th or 50th percentile threshold. Empty regions and regions lacking either band remain unavailable.

7.name: Table_legends
rows: Supplementary Table S7: Broad regional expression profiles and patient-level agreement
The following explanation applies to all data worksheets in this workbook.
Broad regional expression profiles and patient-level agreement

Regional profile differences use broad resource-specific gene panels and log1pCPM profiles. The scaled profile metric divides gene-wise absolute differences by a fixed resource-wide scale (1.4826 times the median absolute deviation, with a 0.25 lower bound); it is different from the earlier four-gene MAD-standardized readout. Patients are the independent units: section pairs are summarized within patient, and between-patient pairwise distances are dependent because pairs share patients. Matched-spot sampling uses 50 deterministic repeats; uncertainty summaries use 2,000 patient-bootstrap draws. These are descriptive sensitivity and uncertainty summaries, not confirmatory tests. For far-minus-near comparisons, a positive scaled absolute difference means greater dissimilarity in far tissue; a positive Spearman correlation difference means greater similarity in far tissue.

8.name: Table_legends
rows: Supplementary Table S8: Author-inferred composition of regions and selected domains
The following explanation applies to all data worksheets in this workbook.
Author-inferred composition of regions and selected domains

The epithelial/proliferating operational group includes the source myeloid-labeled Proliferating subtype. Mean inferred-abundance summaries come from the same RNA-based cell2location reference model and do not constitute cell-resolved validation in this cohort. The added sensitivity stratifies on the model's dominant inferred group after earlier outcomes were known. Common-spot quotas are used only for immune and epithelial_or_proliferating groups. This finite procedure does not balance true or continuous composition and does not establish sufficient composition balance. Four patients have target counts of 49, 103, 23 and 105 spots, respectively; 200 draws were attempted and accepted. The q05 arm is the lower-summary-weight output only, not a complete uncertainty interval. Missing joins and unavailable regional summaries remain missing and are not imputed. Mean inferred abundance divides summed inferred abundance by the number of matched spots. Relative modeled share divides a group's summed abundance by summed abundance across all 36 reference populations. Entire selected domains and their annotated-stroma intersections are summarized separately.

The regional contrast is the median expression among near spots minus the median among far spots. Its exploratory four-gene readout is the arithmetic mean of log1p CP10K expression for TGFB1, CXCL12, ACTA2 and TAGLN. “Expression units” refer to this mean or the named component. The supporting tables describe the tissue and expression contributing to each tumor-adjacent versus distant stromal comparison. The regional contrast is the median expression among near spots minus the median among far spots. Its exploratory four-gene readout is the arithmetic mean of log1p CP10K expression for TGFB1, CXCL12, ACTA2 and TAGLN. “Expression units” refer to this mean or the named component. Standardized values divide by the median absolute deviation (MAD) across all annotated pure stromal spots in the section. A zero MAD makes standardized values undefined; expression-unit estimates remain available when the tissue requirements are met.

The 22 attempted sections represent 12 patients; the baseline domain-selected comparisons draw on five patients per resource. Patient counts remain the unit of biological replication across maps, sections, graphs and sensitivity settings. Tables report the observations contributing to each contrast, standardized estimate or whole-domain geometry. Complete row grids retain unavailable attempts, with status fields indicating the tissue or fitting requirements and NA indicating missing or inapplicable quantities. The field dictionary defines columns, units and missing values.
Detection and dispersion help explain each component's regional contrast.

Seven readouts comprise the four-gene mean, its individual genes and the two paired-gene means. component_expression_summary.tsv gives their near and far medians, all-stroma MAD and fraction of positive stromal values for each section and graph. Detection fractions show how sparse expression contributes to a zero MAD, which prevents standardization even when some spots express the gene. regional_patient_sensitivity.tsv and regional_resource_summary.tsv report component contrasts and reference comparisons under both sets of regional requirements and all declared settings. Resource medians give equal weight to available patients after the within-patient aggregation. The distributions help interpret differences between component contrasts, particularly when many stromal spots have zero expression.

10.name: Table_legends
rows: The supporting tables describe the tissue and expression contributing to each tumor-adjacent versus distant stromal comparison. The regional contrast is the median expression among near spots minus the median among far spots. Its exploratory four-gene readout is the arithmetic mean of log1p CP10K expression for TGFB1, CXCL12, ACTA2 and TAGLN. “Expression units” refer to this mean or the named component. Standardized values divide by the median absolute deviation (MAD) across all annotated pure stromal spots in the section. A zero MAD makes standardized values undefined; expression-unit estimates remain available when the tissue requirements are met.
See Table_legends and Field_dictionary for definitions.

The supporting tables describe the tissue and expression contributing to each tumor-adjacent versus distant stromal comparison. The regional contrast is the median expression among near spots minus the median among far spots. Its exploratory four-gene readout is the arithmetic mean of log1p CP10K expression for TGFB1, CXCL12, ACTA2 and TAGLN. “Expression units” refer to this mean or the named component. Standardized values divide by the median absolute deviation (MAD) across all annotated pure stromal spots in the section. A zero MAD makes standardized values undefined; expression-unit estimates remain available when the tissue requirements are met.

The 22 attempted sections represent 12 patients; the baseline domain-selected comparisons draw on five patients per resource. Patient counts remain the unit of biological replication across maps, sections, graphs and sensitivity settings. Tables report the observations contributing to each contrast, standardized estimate or whole-domain geometry. Complete row grids retain unavailable attempts, with status fields indicating the tissue or fitting requirements and NA indicating missing or inapplicable quantities. The field dictionary defines columns, units and missing values.
The annotated tissue available for each section's regional contrast.

Counts of near and far stromal spots and occupied blocks show which sections supply enough tissue for a full-band comparison. Contrast estimates are accompanied by percentile spatial-block bootstrap intervals; full_band_supported additionally applies the stated MAD margin. The 22 baseline section records are in anchor_section_summary.tsv, and corrected_anchor_all_settings.tsv evaluates them under two graphs and five spatial settings. diagnostic_section_summary.tsv gives section-level results for maps eligible for comparison with their default maps under the fixed criteria based on image-pixel distances. The counts show why a section can lack a full-band contrast even when it contains annotated stroma.

11.name: Table_legends
rows: The supporting tables describe the tissue and expression contributing to each tumor-adjacent versus distant stromal comparison. The regional contrast is the median expression among near spots minus the median among far spots. Its exploratory four-gene readout is the arithmetic mean of log1p CP10K expression for TGFB1, CXCL12, ACTA2 and TAGLN. “Expression units” refer to this mean or the named component. Standardized values divide by the median absolute deviation (MAD) across all annotated pure stromal spots in the section. A zero MAD makes standardized values undefined; expression-unit estimates remain available when the tissue requirements are met.
See Table_legends and Field_dictionary for definitions.

The supporting tables describe the tissue and expression contributing to each tumor-adjacent versus distant stromal comparison. The regional contrast is the median expression among near spots minus the median among far spots. Its exploratory four-gene readout is the arithmetic mean of log1p CP10K expression for TGFB1, CXCL12, ACTA2 and TAGLN. “Expression units” refer to this mean or the named component. Standardized values divide by the median absolute deviation (MAD) across all annotated pure stromal spots in the section. A zero MAD makes standardized values undefined; expression-unit estimates remain available when the tissue requirements are met.

The 22 attempted sections represent 12 patients; the baseline domain-selected comparisons draw on five patients per resource. Patient counts remain the unit of biological replication across maps, sections, graphs and sensitivity settings. Tables report the observations contributing to each contrast, standardized estimate or whole-domain geometry. Complete row grids retain unavailable attempts, with status fields indicating the tissue or fitting requirements and NA indicating missing or inapplicable quantities. The field dictionary defines columns, units and missing values.
How each saved domain changes the regional tissue and expression comparison.

Near and far retention fractions show the selected-band counts relative to the complete annotated bands. Whole-domain stromal fraction describes composition before intersection with either band. current_per_map_results.tsv includes all 1,680 baseline map-by-selection-rule combinations. Across both rules, 665 meet the regional tissue requirements, including 407 primary stromal-retention records: 261 GSE294385 and 146 Valdeolivas. Its status assesses each selection on its own bands. The historical_status field identifies combinations eligible for comparison with the default map under the fixed criteria based on image-pixel distances, as described in Supporting Methods. Full-band, selected-domain and paired-change interval fields each retain their own availability.
How each saved domain changes the regional tissue and expression comparison.

The reference-map sensitivity gives estimates for maps eligible for comparison with their default maps under the fixed criteria based on image-pixel distances. diagnostic_map_diagnostic.tsv retains the same 1,680 keys with continuous contrasts and controls. Its status and diagnostic_status impose these fixed reference-map eligibility criteria, leaving 582 combinations across both rules. Its status fields distinguish this narrower set from maps meeting their own regional tissue requirements. Own-band controls are in the primary-readout baseline subset of Table S12 (regional_map_sensitivity.tsv), under array-coordinate six-neighbor connectivity and independent_status. Each reference uses 1,000 subset draws; its 2.5th/97.5th percentile envelope describes the distribution of subset departures. diagnostic_status_summary.tsv and diagnostic_method_k_summary.tsv describe availability under this fixed reference-map eligibility and setting/readout summaries beyond baseline. Tables S1 and S13 summarize the resulting patient estimates and purity screening.

12.name: Table_legends
rows: The supporting tables describe the tissue and expression contributing to each tumor-adjacent versus distant stromal comparison. The regional contrast is the median expression among near spots minus the median among far spots. Its exploratory four-gene readout is the arithmetic mean of log1p CP10K expression for TGFB1, CXCL12, ACTA2 and TAGLN. “Expression units” refer to this mean or the named component. Standardized values divide by the median absolute deviation (MAD) across all annotated pure stromal spots in the section. A zero MAD makes standardized values undefined; expression-unit estimates remain available when the tissue requirements are met.
See Table_legends and Field_dictionary for definitions.

The supporting tables describe the tissue and expression contributing to each tumor-adjacent versus distant stromal comparison. The regional contrast is the median expression among near spots minus the median among far spots. Its exploratory four-gene readout is the arithmetic mean of log1p CP10K expression for TGFB1, CXCL12, ACTA2 and TAGLN. “Expression units” refer to this mean or the named component. Standardized values divide by the median absolute deviation (MAD) across all annotated pure stromal spots in the section. A zero MAD makes standardized values undefined; expression-unit estimates remain available when the tissue requirements are met.

The 22 attempted sections represent 12 patients; the baseline domain-selected comparisons draw on five patients per resource. Patient counts remain the unit of biological replication across maps, sections, graphs and sensitivity settings. Tables report the observations contributing to each contrast, standardized estimate or whole-domain geometry. Complete row grids retain unavailable attempts, with status fields indicating the tissue or fitting requirements and NA indicating missing or inapplicable quantities. The field dictionary defines columns, units and missing values.
Component expression across spatial definitions and regional selections.

Contrast estimates are accompanied by the tissue and patient counts contributing to each comparison. regional_map_sensitivity.tsv contains 36,960 records: the four-gene readout under two graphs and five settings, plus six component readouts at baseline under both graphs. The six regional_*_method_k_sensitivity.tsv, regional_*_section_sensitivity.tsv and regional_*_patient_sensitivity.tsv files summarize each step from partitions to patients. They cover both selections assessed on their own bands and the “Reference-eligible subset” shown in Fig S4. Supporting Methods define the fixed image-coordinate eligibility requirements for comparison with a default map. Counts separately identify attempted configurations, those with sufficient regional tissue and those with defined MAD-scaled estimates. Each readout, graph, setting and comparison frame has its own denominator.

13.name: Table_legends
rows: The supporting tables describe the tissue and expression contributing to each tumor-adjacent versus distant stromal comparison. The regional contrast is the median expression among near spots minus the median among far spots. Its exploratory four-gene readout is the arithmetic mean of log1p CP10K expression for TGFB1, CXCL12, ACTA2 and TAGLN. “Expression units” refer to this mean or the named component. Standardized values divide by the median absolute deviation (MAD) across all annotated pure stromal spots in the section. A zero MAD makes standardized values undefined; expression-unit estimates remain available when the tissue requirements are met.
See Table_legends and Field_dictionary for definitions.

The supporting tables describe the tissue and expression contributing to each tumor-adjacent versus distant stromal comparison. The regional contrast is the median expression among near spots minus the median among far spots. Its exploratory four-gene readout is the arithmetic mean of log1p CP10K expression for TGFB1, CXCL12, ACTA2 and TAGLN. “Expression units” refer to this mean or the named component. Standardized values divide by the median absolute deviation (MAD) across all annotated pure stromal spots in the section. A zero MAD makes standardized values undefined; expression-unit estimates remain available when the tissue requirements are met.

The 22 attempted sections represent 12 patients; the baseline domain-selected comparisons draw on five patients per resource. Patient counts remain the unit of biological replication across maps, sections, graphs and sensitivity settings. Tables report the observations contributing to each contrast, standardized estimate or whole-domain geometry. Complete row grids retain unavailable attempts, with status fields indicating the tissue or fitting requirements and NA indicating missing or inapplicable quantities. The field dictionary defines columns, units and missing values.
Greater whole-domain stromal purity can reduce regional coverage.

Screening at minimum stromal fractions of 0, 0.50 and 0.75 changes which domains still contain sufficient near and far tissue. primary_stromal_fraction_summary.tsv reports those domains, sections and patients separately. Fig 2 reports medians across retained map configurations alongside their counts. Purity refers to the whole molecular domain; the expression comparison itself uses its annotated stromal intersections. regional_purity_sensitivity.tsv covers both sets of regional requirements, graphs, settings and readouts. diagnostic_purity_sensitivity.tsv gives the reference-map-restricted baseline comparison. Spot, section and patient counts show how the contributing tissue changes with each threshold.

14.name: Table_legends
rows: The supporting tables describe the tissue and expression contributing to each tumor-adjacent versus distant stromal comparison. The regional contrast is the median expression among near spots minus the median among far spots. Its exploratory four-gene readout is the arithmetic mean of log1p CP10K expression for TGFB1, CXCL12, ACTA2 and TAGLN. “Expression units” refer to this mean or the named component. Standardized values divide by the median absolute deviation (MAD) across all annotated pure stromal spots in the section. A zero MAD makes standardized values undefined; expression-unit estimates remain available when the tissue requirements are met.
See Table_legends and Field_dictionary for definitions.

The supporting tables describe the tissue and expression contributing to each tumor-adjacent versus distant stromal comparison. The regional contrast is the median expression among near spots minus the median among far spots. Its exploratory four-gene readout is the arithmetic mean of log1p CP10K expression for TGFB1, CXCL12, ACTA2 and TAGLN. “Expression units” refer to this mean or the named component. Standardized values divide by the median absolute deviation (MAD) across all annotated pure stromal spots in the section. A zero MAD makes standardized values undefined; expression-unit estimates remain available when the tissue requirements are met.

The 22 attempted sections represent 12 patients; the baseline domain-selected comparisons draw on five patients per resource. Patient counts remain the unit of biological replication across maps, sections, graphs and sensitivity settings. Tables report the observations contributing to each contrast, standardized estimate or whole-domain geometry. Complete row grids retain unavailable attempts, with status fields indicating the tissue or fitting requirements and NA indicating missing or inapplicable quantities. The field dictionary defines columns, units and missing values.
Domain movement inside and outside the measured tissue bands.

The table locates changes in selected stromal membership relative to the near and far regions. Primary alternatives with changed membership are included under each graph and setting, whether their selections overlap partly or are disjoint. Jaccard overlap is the intersection divided by the union of all selected annotated stromal spots, including those outside the bands. Centroid shifts use nominal-array micrometers. Counts of changed spots outside the bands distinguish movement of the molecular domain from movement entering the regional expression measurement. The records are in domain_repartitioning_summary.tsv.

15.name: Table_legends
rows: The supporting tables describe the tissue and expression contributing to each tumor-adjacent versus distant stromal comparison. The regional contrast is the median expression among near spots minus the median among far spots. Its exploratory four-gene readout is the arithmetic mean of log1p CP10K expression for TGFB1, CXCL12, ACTA2 and TAGLN. “Expression units” refer to this mean or the named component. Standardized values divide by the median absolute deviation (MAD) across all annotated pure stromal spots in the section. A zero MAD makes standardized values undefined; expression-unit estimates remain available when the tissue requirements are met.
See Table_legends and Field_dictionary for definitions.

The supporting tables describe the tissue and expression contributing to each tumor-adjacent versus distant stromal comparison. The regional contrast is the median expression among near spots minus the median among far spots. Its exploratory four-gene readout is the arithmetic mean of log1p CP10K expression for TGFB1, CXCL12, ACTA2 and TAGLN. “Expression units” refer to this mean or the named component. Standardized values divide by the median absolute deviation (MAD) across all annotated pure stromal spots in the section. A zero MAD makes standardized values undefined; expression-unit estimates remain available when the tissue requirements are met.

The 22 attempted sections represent 12 patients; the baseline domain-selected comparisons draw on five patients per resource. Patient counts remain the unit of biological replication across maps, sections, graphs and sensitivity settings. Tables report the observations contributing to each contrast, standardized estimate or whole-domain geometry. Complete row grids retain unavailable attempts, with status fields indicating the tissue or fitting requirements and NA indicating missing or inapplicable quantities. The field dictionary defines columns, units and missing values.
Regional tissue and matched-subset departures depend on spatial definition.

The table compares the detail preserved by spatial matching and the connectivity used to define the stromal bands. spatial_scale_summary.tsv reports four-gene summaries under two graphs and five settings, with patient, section and configuration counts before and after regional screening. graph_band_membership_summary.tsv identifies baseline membership differences between array-coordinate six-neighbor connectivity and exact hexagonal adjacency. With the nominal 100-micrometer pitch, near limits of 100 and 150 micrometers include the same first lattice ring. Their memberships are therefore identical, although setting-specific random subsets can give different control summaries. Supporting Methods define the distances, grids and graphs; the wider near-band comparison is in Table S16.

16.name: Table_legends
rows: The supporting tables describe the tissue and expression contributing to each tumor-adjacent versus distant stromal comparison. The regional contrast is the median expression among near spots minus the median among far spots. Its exploratory four-gene readout is the arithmetic mean of log1p CP10K expression for TGFB1, CXCL12, ACTA2 and TAGLN. “Expression units” refer to this mean or the named component. Standardized values divide by the median absolute deviation (MAD) across all annotated pure stromal spots in the section. A zero MAD makes standardized values undefined; expression-unit estimates remain available when the tissue requirements are met.
See Table_legends and Field_dictionary for definitions.

The supporting tables describe the tissue and expression contributing to each tumor-adjacent versus distant stromal comparison. The regional contrast is the median expression among near spots minus the median among far spots. Its exploratory four-gene readout is the arithmetic mean of log1p CP10K expression for TGFB1, CXCL12, ACTA2 and TAGLN. “Expression units” refer to this mean or the named component. Standardized values divide by the median absolute deviation (MAD) across all annotated pure stromal spots in the section. A zero MAD makes standardized values undefined; expression-unit estimates remain available when the tissue requirements are met.

The 22 attempted sections represent 12 patients; the baseline domain-selected comparisons draw on five patients per resource. Patient counts remain the unit of biological replication across maps, sections, graphs and sensitivity settings. Tables report the observations contributing to each contrast, standardized estimate or whole-domain geometry. Complete row grids retain unavailable attempts, with status fields indicating the tissue or fitting requirements and NA indicating missing or inapplicable quantities. The field dictionary defines columns, units and missing values.
Admitting the second lattice ring changes the anatomical target.

A near limit of 175 micrometers includes the second hexagonal ring at approximately 173.2 micrometers. Far distances remain 200-400 micrometers. Final far membership can nevertheless change because a far spot must lie in a stromal component containing a near spot. Both graphs, both selection rules and all saved configurations are evaluated. wider_near_map_results.tsv, wider_near_anchor_intervals.tsv and wider_near_membership.tsv report the resulting contrasts, full-band intervals and section memberships.
Admitting the second lattice ring changes the anatomical target.

The paired-setting summaries distinguish a change within the same maps from the availability of new regional comparisons. near_band_map_comparison.tsv places all 3,360 map, selection-rule and graph combinations side by side at 100 and 175 micrometers and identifies those meeting requirements in both. near_band_common_map_summary.tsv gives 16 summaries by resource, graph, selection rule and band over those common configurations. wider_near_patient_summary.tsv and wider_near_resource_summary.tsv use the primary own-band patient hierarchy. Each available record receives 1,000 new subsets under each reference construction. Full-band contrasts have both separate-band and common-block intervals. Selected-map and paired-change outputs for this wider target contain point contrasts and matched-subset summaries, with interval fields unavailable.

17.name: Table_legends
rows: The supporting tables describe the tissue and expression contributing to each tumor-adjacent versus distant stromal comparison. The regional contrast is the median expression among near spots minus the median among far spots. Its exploratory four-gene readout is the arithmetic mean of log1p CP10K expression for TGFB1, CXCL12, ACTA2 and TAGLN. “Expression units” refer to this mean or the named component. Standardized values divide by the median absolute deviation (MAD) across all annotated pure stromal spots in the section. A zero MAD makes standardized values undefined; expression-unit estimates remain available when the tissue requirements are met.
See Table_legends and Field_dictionary for definitions.

The supporting tables describe the tissue and expression contributing to each tumor-adjacent versus distant stromal comparison. The regional contrast is the median expression among near spots minus the median among far spots. Its exploratory four-gene readout is the arithmetic mean of log1p CP10K expression for TGFB1, CXCL12, ACTA2 and TAGLN. “Expression units” refer to this mean or the named component. Standardized values divide by the median absolute deviation (MAD) across all annotated pure stromal spots in the section. A zero MAD makes standardized values undefined; expression-unit estimates remain available when the tissue requirements are met.

The 22 attempted sections represent 12 patients; the baseline domain-selected comparisons draw on five patients per resource. Patient counts remain the unit of biological replication across maps, sections, graphs and sensitivity settings. Tables report the observations contributing to each contrast, standardized estimate or whole-domain geometry. Complete row grids retain unavailable attempts, with status fields indicating the tissue or fitting requirements and NA indicating missing or inapplicable quantities. The field dictionary defines columns, units and missing values.
Map families select different regional representations of annotated stroma.

The table compares the tissue retained by each map family and the regional contrast it represents. method_selection_comparison.tsv reports baseline four-gene results by resource, selection rule and method. Patient summaries use partition medians within K and section, equal K weights within sections and equal section weights within patients; the table gives their medians. Contrast counts require sufficient spots and blocks, and standardized counts additionally require nonzero stromal MAD. Whole-domain Jaccard and centroid summaries use available alternative geometries. Their configuration, section and patient counts are reported separately and can exceed those for regional contrasts. map_producer_parameters.tsv gives actual preprocessing, spatial representation and fitting settings, including neural and Bayesian software calls.

18.name: Table_legends
rows: The supporting tables describe the tissue and expression contributing to each tumor-adjacent versus distant stromal comparison. The regional contrast is the median expression among near spots minus the median among far spots. Its exploratory four-gene readout is the arithmetic mean of log1p CP10K expression for TGFB1, CXCL12, ACTA2 and TAGLN. “Expression units” refer to this mean or the named component. Standardized values divide by the median absolute deviation (MAD) across all annotated pure stromal spots in the section. A zero MAD makes standardized values undefined; expression-unit estimates remain available when the tissue requirements are met.
See Table_legends and Field_dictionary for definitions.

The supporting tables describe the tissue and expression contributing to each tumor-adjacent versus distant stromal comparison. The regional contrast is the median expression among near spots minus the median among far spots. Its exploratory four-gene readout is the arithmetic mean of log1p CP10K expression for TGFB1, CXCL12, ACTA2 and TAGLN. “Expression units” refer to this mean or the named component. Standardized values divide by the median absolute deviation (MAD) across all annotated pure stromal spots in the section. A zero MAD makes standardized values undefined; expression-unit estimates remain available when the tissue requirements are met.

The 22 attempted sections represent 12 patients; the baseline domain-selected comparisons draw on five patients per resource. Patient counts remain the unit of biological replication across maps, sections, graphs and sensitivity settings. Tables report the observations contributing to each contrast, standardized estimate or whole-domain geometry. Complete row grids retain unavailable attempts, with status fields indicating the tissue or fitting requirements and NA indicating missing or inapplicable quantities. The field dictionary defines columns, units and missing values.
Shared block sampling can change an interval around the same regional contrast.

The two constructions estimate the same difference of pooled-spot medians. The separate-band procedure samples occupied near and far blocks separately; the common-block procedure samples their union and applies each sampled block's multiplicity to both bands. common_block_intervals.tsv retains all 220 attempted full-band comparisons from 22 sections, two graphs and five grid/band settings. Attempts, accepted draws and rejections for an empty band are recorded. Width ratios divide the common-block interval width by the separate-band width. Shared multiplicities also change marginal block weights and the number of pooled spots, so the comparison reflects these changes together. The sensitivity comparison concerns full-band intervals; selected-map and paired-change intervals retain the constructions defined in Supporting Methods.

19.name: Table_legends
rows: The supporting tables describe the tissue and expression contributing to each tumor-adjacent versus distant stromal comparison. The regional contrast is the median expression among near spots minus the median among far spots. Its exploratory four-gene readout is the arithmetic mean of log1p CP10K expression for TGFB1, CXCL12, ACTA2 and TAGLN. “Expression units” refer to this mean or the named component. Standardized values divide by the median absolute deviation (MAD) across all annotated pure stromal spots in the section. A zero MAD makes standardized values undefined; expression-unit estimates remain available when the tissue requirements are met.
See Table_legends and Field_dictionary for definitions.

The supporting tables describe the tissue and expression contributing to each tumor-adjacent versus distant stromal comparison. The regional contrast is the median expression among near spots minus the median among far spots. Its exploratory four-gene readout is the arithmetic mean of log1p CP10K expression for TGFB1, CXCL12, ACTA2 and TAGLN. “Expression units” refer to this mean or the named component. Standardized values divide by the median absolute deviation (MAD) across all annotated pure stromal spots in the section. A zero MAD makes standardized values undefined; expression-unit estimates remain available when the tissue requirements are met.

The 22 attempted sections represent 12 patients; the baseline domain-selected comparisons draw on five patients per resource. Patient counts remain the unit of biological replication across maps, sections, graphs and sensitivity settings. Tables report the observations contributing to each contrast, standardized estimate or whole-domain geometry. Complete row grids retain unavailable attempts, with status fields indicating the tissue or fitting requirements and NA indicating missing or inapplicable quantities. The field dictionary defines columns, units and missing values.
Interval performance and classification when the regional signal is known.

Prescribed maps and known targets allow sampling error to be distinguished from actual signal change. The simulation contains 52 conditions and 5,200 realizations in simulation_cell_metrics.tsv. simulation_summary.tsv reports availability, bias, root mean squared error (RMSE), interval coverage and null rejection by condition, map and target. Coverage and rate bounds are 95% Wilson intervals across noise realizations within each fixed finite-grid condition. simulation_calibration_by_map.tsv applies the stated calibration screens, and simulation_threshold_sensitivity.tsv gives numerators and denominators for each support rule. Four/eight-neighbor conditions change majority smoothing of the prescribed labels; stricter regional selection retains six-neighbor adjacency. Identical masks give exact zero paired intervals and are excluded from nondegenerate paired calibration. The reference displacement selects identical spots under both rules in all 52 conditions; the alternative displacement gives different selections in 51. Equal reference rates therefore represent the same regional measurement. Interval performance is assessed against the known targets of these prescribed finite-grid conditions.
